You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From dfbc282c2e16cd6044e4181f150dbd1e2224eaa7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Masatake YAMATO <yamato@redhat.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2014 11:49:17 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] check multiple parser methods are not defined in a parser

This fixes a bug introduced in be4a2117494ce73750cec3fd3c7cb4a60e722bcf.

The old commit(be4a21) checked only the case that allparser, parser2 and parser_with_gc
were not set but didn't check more than one were set. This patch checks this case, too.

Signed-off-by: Masatake YAMATO <yamato@redhat.com>

diff --git a/parse.c b/parse.c
index 557228d1d..2ae586ea0 100644
--- a/parse.c
+++ b/parse.c
@@ -969,7 +969,7 @@ extern void initializeParsing (void)
 				accepted = TRUE;
 #endif
 			}
-			else if ((def->parser == NULL)  &&  (def->parser2 == NULL) && (def->parser_with_gc == NULL))
+			else if (((!!def->parser) + (!!def->parser2) + (!!def->parser_with_gc)) != 1)
 				error (FATAL,
 		"%s parser definition must define one and only one parsing routine\n",
 					   def->name);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `parse.c`**
- The conditional check in the `initializeParsing` function was modified. 
- The original check verified that all three parser methods (`parser`, `parser2`, and `parser_with_gc`) were not set to `NULL`. 
- The new check ensures that exactly one of these parser methods is defined. It uses a sum of boolean values to determine if one and only one parser method is set, replacing the previous check.

### Relationships
- The modification in `parse.c` addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (be4a21) that only checked if none of the parser methods were defined. The new logic ensures that the parser definitions are validated correctly, enforcing that only one parser method can be defined at a time, thus preventing potential conflicts or undefined behavior in the parsing process.

1. analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 
2. output the file name that is most likely to cause the bug.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
else if ((def->parser == NULL)  &&  (def->parser2 == NULL) && (def->parser_with_gc == NULL))
```
Reason:
This statement only checks if all parser methods (`parser`, `parser2`, and `parser_with_gc`) are unset, allowing the possibility of multiple parser methods being defined simultaneously without raising an error. This insufficient validation can lead to ambiguity in parsing behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
else if (((!!def->parser) + (!!def->parser2) + (!!def->parser_with_gc)) != 1)
```
Reason:
This updated condition checks that exactly one of the parser methods is defined by summing the truth values of each parser method. If the sum is not equal to one, it raises an error, thus enforcing the rule that only one parser method can be defined at a time and preventing potential parsing errors.
